evidence_required: route and generated OpenAPI contract output
stable no-leak error and redaction evidence
named uniqueness-race versus generic persistence failure-injection evidence
focused API, API regression, and full pytest output
constraints: Reuse the existing FastAPI app factory, FT-001 session/ActorContext dependencies, error envelope, and persisted FT-002 services.
Do not expose a bootstrap HTTP endpoint or implement FT-003 admin projections, retained history, UI, downstream operations, or agent flows.
Do not return raw model objects, SQL errors, auth material, or existence-revealing Plant errors.
Request models must forbid immutable/server-owned fields and unknown fields.
FarmService must classify a Plant-key race only from a precheck or positive named-constraint match; the API must not infer conflict from a generic persistence failure.
invariants: Backend authorization is authoritative; frontend visibility is presentation only.
Unknown, unauthorized, revoked/missing-grant, and archived normal Plant paths share the safe no-leak denial.
Archived Plant lifecycle/access administration is a narrow Boss exception and never normal operational access.
can_approve_actions is actor authority only and never Safety Gate clearance.
Stable error codes remain truthful: generic DB/audit/flush/commit failures never become PLANT_KEY_CONFLICT from route context alone.
Entity-specific persistence errors remain truthful: Farm mutations never return Plant-specific fallback codes or messages.
verification_targets: Inspect generated OpenAPI against every canonical FT-002 path, body, response, enum, UUID, timestamp, and error status.
Prove route results and denial filtering use persisted Plant/grant rows through ActorContext.
Inject the named Plant-key uniqueness race and an unrelated persistence failure; prove distinct stable codes, full rollback, no success audits, and redacted bodies.
Inject PATCH /api/farm persistence failure and prove FARM_PERSISTENCE_FAILED HTTP 500 while the Plant persistence failure path still returns PLANT_PERSISTENCE_FAILED.
purpose: Expose the completed FT-002 authority and lifecycle services through one exact protected HTTP boundary usable by later admin and PWA features.
success_outcome: Authorized actors can use the canonical Farm, Plant lifecycle, and access-grant API with exact no-leak errors and no frontend-only authorization dependency.
anti_goals: No retained-history or downstream operations routes.

stop_conditions: TASK-013-T3-FT-002-W2 is not done or its service/permission contract differs from canonical specs.
A route would require frontend-only authorization or existence-revealing errors.
The canonical HTTP contract cannot be represented by generated schemas/OpenAPI.
A response or error would expose auth material, raw SQL, or credential-bearing configuration.
The service cannot positively distinguish the named Plant-key unique constraint from generic persistence failure without leaking backend exception details.
